newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks, bounce back, close up for 2nd day.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks, bounce back, close up for 2nd day.

text.p: Caracas stocks continued to bounce back, closing up for the second straight day, traders said, while the bolsa also buzzed with rumors paints company Corimon may be relisted on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).
"There's been a lot talk that its ADRs might be relisted on the NYSE and maybe even its B shares, too," said a broker.

Corimon was suspended from the NYSE and Caracas bolsa in February 1996 on bankruptcy fears. But trading resumed in Venezuela in October after it capitalized much of its $100 million debt into preferred Type B shares.
The bolsa's leading 19-share index gained 0.86 percent to close at 6,317.54 points as 25 million shares exchanged hands, worth three billion bolivars ($6.4 million).
Trade was led by 12 million Corimon B shares. The stock closed flat at 9.25 bolivars.
Among traded issues, 25 rose, nine fell and 18 closed flat. Despite the bounce, traders did not see the rise gaining steam.
"While there's no foreign interest, stocks will continue to be erratic and volume thin," said one broker.
Traders said foreign investors continued to wait on a clearer settlement of Venezuela's on-going labor problems.
Some 2,000 demonstrating Venezuelan public sector workers linked arms Wednesday and made a human chain around Congress in a peaceful protest Wednesday for steep pay rises.

The protest is the latest in a series of labor conflicts and 100 percent plus pay claims that has roiled the New Year, sparking fears of renewed inflation. However, Finance Minister Luis Raul Matos Azocar, speaking in London, said such claims would not bust the government's 1.3 billion bolivar allowance.
